A new JAMA study published April 16 finds that the death rate in ICE custody for fiscal year 2026 is the highest in 22 years, surpassing even the COVID-19 peak. The data goes back to FY2004. 🧵

If detention population alone explained the deaths, the rate per 100,000 wouldn't rise. It does. Sharply. That's what the JAMA study is measuring. More people in custody is not the same as more people dying per capita, and conflating the two obscures the conditions question.

I've been tracking these deaths facility-by-facility for months. Continuing coverage on my Substack: austinkocher.substack.com/p/…  and at detentionreports.com

Read the report: jamanetwork.com/journals/jam…

There's also a revolving door worth flagging. David Venturella, who recently joined ICE after leaving GEO Group, is now leading the division that oversees detention contracts while GEO bids on warehouse work. Attorney General Pam Bondi is a former GEO lobbyist.

The timeline is aggressive. DHS wants the first warehouse facility accepting detainees this month. Some planned buildings will hold 7,000–10,000 people, rivaling the capacity of Las Vegas resorts and far exceeding the typical 1,800-person existing facility.

DHS fired Acquisition Logistics in March 2026 and replaced them with Amentum Services via a no-bid contract. Public Citizen documented 112 prior regulatory violations against Amentum, including fraud, discrimination, and health and safety issues.

The Camp East Montana facility near El Paso is the cautionary case. The initial $1.3 billion contract went to Acquisition Logistics LLC, which had no prior detention experience. 2 days after the award, a subcontractor employee died at the site. 3 detainees have since died.

GardaWorld Federal Services received at least $313.4 million to run a planned detention center in Surprise, Arizona. GardaWorld employs guards at "Alligator Alcatraz" in Florida and at Canadian immigration facilities, but had not previously been directly contracted by ICE

KVG LLC, a defense contractor based in Gettysburg, PA, was awarded at least $113.1 million to retrofit and operate the 1,500-bed warehouse near Hagerstown, Maryland. Before this contract, KVG had no public record of running an immigration detention facility.

The ICE Detention Reengineering Initiative ($38 billion to convert commercial warehouses into a network of massive detention centers) is not being built primarily by GEO Group and CoreCivic. ICE is turning to a crop of relatively untested contractors. A look at who. 🧵
